conventions.convention: SI coordinates; q is signed and nonzero, M=mc²>0 is rest energy, and Cw=(q/m)w×B in right-handed Cartesian coordinates. Angular frequencies are positive and counted with multiplicity; ordinary frequencies are ω/(2π).
R(a,c)=1+a/c on real a and positive c; c here is the denominator variable, not light speed. Error bounds are deterministic, and the remainder uses the Euclidean norm on R².
The hertz-valued inputs and interval bounds are stipulated hypothetical values, with no empirical or statistical interpretation.

load_bearing.statement: For R(a,c)=1+a/c, c>0, |δa|≤εa and |δc|≤εc<c, with nonnegative bounds, |R(a+δa,c+δc)−R(a,c)|≤(cεa+|a|εc)/(c(c−εc)). If the segment from x=(a,c) to x+h lies in Q=[A−,A+]×[c−,c+] with A−≤A+ and 0<c−≤c+, then Lx(u,v)=u/c−av/c² is the total derivative and |R(x+h)−R(x)−Lx(h)|≤((max(|A−|,|A+|)+c+/2)/c−³)‖h‖₂².

For q≠0, M>0, c>0, constant B≠0, symmetric real K with tr K=0, α=qc²/M, D=−αK, Cw=αw×B, and A(r,v)=(v,Dr+Cv), assume A is diagonalizable over C with eigenvalues ±iωj, j=1,2,3, every ωj>0 counted with multiplicity. Then ωc²=ω1²+ω2²+ω3², where ωc=|q|c²|B|/M; the same squared-sum identity holds for ordinary frequencies ω/(2π).
